howTo.title: How to use
items: Type a name and press Enter, or paste a whole list. For a class, enter the head count to fill numbers from 1.
The loop is drawn as soon as the names are in. Draw again as often as you like, and add couples or family under Don't pair.
Send the group chat link. Everyone taps their own name and opens a gift box that shows only their person.
No phones in class? Show the QR code on a screen, or pass one phone around and check one by one.

items: Leave a warm drink on their desk in the morning

tips.title: Tips
items: Set a budget like 'about 10,000 KRW' so gifts feel balanced.
Enter the reveal day as the exchange date. From that day the group link can show everyone’s pairs together.
Changing names or drawing again changes the assignment. Finalize the list before sending links.
If the organizer plays too, don't expand the full result. Open the link you sent and tap your own name.
Because it's one loop, if A has B, B never has A, so no awkward mutual pairs.

items.a: Each person secretly looks after one other person for a while, and on the last day everyone reveals who had whom. It's popular for classes, clubs, year-end parties and Christmas.

items.q: Is one link in the group chat enough?
items.a: Yes. Everyone picks their own name and opens only their person, and a chosen name stays fixed on that device. There is no login, so it can't stop someone from tapping another name on a different device. If it must stay secret, send personal links one by one.
Ask the organizer for your personal link under Send one by one.

items.q: Can the organizer see the result?
items.a: The organizer sees only the list and share buttons; the full result appears only when you expand 'Show the full result'. If you're also playing, don't expand it and open only your own name.

items.q: Are names in the link? Is anything stored on a server?
items.a: The assignment is obscured after the # in the link, and that part is never sent to the server. ToolHub stores no lists or results; the organizer's last list and the name you picked stay only in each browser. It's obscured, not encrypted.
Pick two people who shouldn't be each other's Santa and tap Add. They won't be linked in either direction. With 3 people everyone is linked, so any rule makes the draw impossible.
From 3 to 50. One link covers a whole class.

items.q: What happens to links I already sent if I draw again?
items.a: Drawing again makes a new assignment, while links already sent keep showing the old one. If the list changes after sending, a notice lets you send a new link or restore the draw you sent.
